questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’

Over two hundred years ago, early in the eighteenth century, our ancestors __had come down over this__ mountain valley to seek fame and fortune in the rich plains below.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence refers to an action completed over two hundred years ago, which requires the past tense construction.
 
• The correct phrase is "**came down from that mountain valley**," which aligns with the context and maintains grammatical accuracy.
 
• Using "**had been coming down onto**" introduces unnecessary complexity and alters the meaning.
 
• The phrase "**comes down into this**" is incorrect because it uses the present tense, which does not fit the timeline of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct substitution is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Over two hundred years ago, early in the eighteenth century, our ancestors **came down from that **mountain valley to seek fame and fortune in the rich plains below."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **No substitution required** – This option would be correct if the original sentence was grammatically accurate, but it is not.
 
• **Option 1: "comes down into this"** – This option is incorrect as it changes the tense to present, which is inconsistent with the timeline of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "had been coming down onto"** – This option is incorrect as it unnecessarily complicates the sentence and alters the meaning.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He has a knack for __ignoring problems intentionally__ in his department, hoping they will just go away.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. 'turning a blind eye'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"turning a blind eye"** means to pretend not to notice something bad happening, or to deliberately ignore something. (अनदेखी करना / नज़रअंदाज करना)

 
 
• **Example:** The principal was accused of turning a blind eye to bullying in the school.
 
 
 
• **"Ignoring problems intentionally"** means to deliberately overlook or disregard issues. (समस्याओं को जानबूझकर नज़रअंदाज करना)
 
 
• **Example:** He was known for ignoring problems intentionally rather than addressing them directly.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom **'turning a blind eye'** aptly substitutes the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **turning a blind eye**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Turning point** (टर्निंग पॉइंट): A time at which a decisive change in a situation occurs.

 
 
• **Example:** The invention of the internet was a turning point in modern history.
 
 
 
• **Turning a leaf** (नया पन्ना पलटना): This could mean starting fresh or making a significant change in behavior.
 
 
• **Example:** He decided to turn a new leaf and start a healthy lifestyle.
 
 
 
• **Turning a corner** (कोने से मुड़ना): To pass a critical point in a process or situation and begin to improve.
 
 
• **Example:** After months of hard work, the company is finally turning a corner.
